`case_study:novo-nordisk-glp1-2016-2026` · tickers US-NVO · confidence: verified

Novo pioneered GLP-1s (Victoza 2010, Ozempic 2017, Wegovy for obesity June 2021). Rise: STEP-1 (Feb 2021, ~15% weight loss), Wegovy launch June 2021 with supply shortages for two years, SELECT (Aug 2023, ~20% fewer heart events). The stock roughly quadrupled from 2021 [approx] and Novo became Europe's most valuable company, worth >$600-650bn at the June 2024 peak — more than Denmark's GDP; ADR ~$145-150 (2:1 split Sep 2023) [unverified]. Mostly EPS growth (sales/EPS growing 20-30%+), with P/E expanding to ~40-45x [unverified]. Reversal: Dec 20 2024 CagriSema trial disappointment -20% (record one-day fall); Lilly's tirzepatide took 63% of US branded obesity scripts by Q3 2025; compounded semaglutide eroded cash pay; CEO Lars Fruergaard Jørgensen ousted May 16 2025 (shares -59% from June 2024 high at that point); new CEO Mike Doustdar cut 9,000 jobs (Sept 2025); Nov 2025 US pricing deal cut government prices; 2026 guidance: first sales decline in modern history (-5% to -13%); Feb 23 2026 CagriSema lost head-to-head vs tirzepatide, -16%, shares at lowest since June 2021 — ~$475bn (~73%) wiped. EARLY SIGNAL (up): Wegovy shortages = demand exceeding supply for 2+ years. EARLY SIGNAL (down): SURPASS/SURMOUNT data showing a better competitor molecule plus Lilly out-investing in capacity, and Novo's next-gen data underwhelming in Dec 2024. LESSON: the category creator does not automatically own the category; peak valuation coincided with peak scarcity, and a superior fast follower plus price normalisation erased the whole Wegovy-era gain.

- **Start → end:** pre-Wegovy levels (~2021) → back to June 2021 levels (Feb 2026) (~4x up (2021-24) [approx], fully round-tripped)
- **EPS vs rerating:** up: EPS + P/E to ~40x; down: P/E collapse + EPS cuts
- **Max drawdown:** ~-73% (Jun 2024-Feb 2026)
- **Early signal:** up: Wegovy shortages; down: Lilly superior data, CagriSema miss Dec 2024
- **Who caught it:** broad European/US growth funds; no documented single name
- **Ended/stalled:** June 2024 peak
- **Lesson:** category creator lost to faster follower; peak scarcity = peak price
- **Sources:** [1](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/novo-nordisks-475-billion-rise-165509914.html) · [2](https://bnnbloomberg.ca/business/company-news/2024/12/20/novo-nordisk-falls-most-on-record-after-new-weight-drug-disappoints) · [3](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/novo-nordisk-ceo-weight-loss-drug-wegovy-to-step-down) · [4](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2025/5/16/in-surprise-move-wegovy-maker-novo-nordisk-ousts-ceo-amid-sagging-sales) · [5](https://philippdubach.com/posts/novo-was-europes-most-valuable-company/)

`strategy:templeton-max-pessimism` | confidence: **single-source** | tags: global, process, contrarian, value

Process: (1) Search everywhere - all countries and industries - for the lowest price relative to long-term earnings power (he used P/E vs history, and P/E vs growth). (2) Buy at 'maximum pessimism': when news is worst and selling is indiscriminate. (3) Diversify across many bargains, because some cheap stocks are cheap for good reason. (4) Sell when a holding's price approaches fair value or a much better bargain appears (he typically held ~4-5 years). (5) Use his cycle ladder - pessimism, skepticism, optimism, euphoria - to judge where a market is. Indian application: years of extreme pessimism (2001-03 post-KP crash, Oct 2008-Mar 2009, Aug 2013 rupee crisis, Mar 2020) all offered P/Es near 11-17x and market cap/GDP near or below 60-75%, followed by 15-30%+ annual returns; a staged buying plan keyed to those valuation levels is the individual's version. Risks: value traps; acting at 'maximum pessimism' requires cash and nerves on hand before the crash.

Links: person:john-templeton (about); insight:india-valuation-forward-returns (about)

Sources: <https://www.caproasia.com/?p=13086> ; <https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/templetons-way-with/9781118149614/xhtml/Chapter03.html>

`insight:marks-ai-bubble-and-layman-2025-26` | confidence: verified | date: 2026-11-11

'Is It a Bubble?' (9 Dec 2025): transformational technologies have 'a consistent history' of 'excessive enthusiasm and investment, resulting in more infrastructure than is needed and asset prices that prove to have been too high', though the excess speeds adoption. Differences from 2000: AI products exist at scale with fast-rising revenue, and leader P/Es are below 1998-2000 Microsoft/Cisco/Oracle levels (Goldman data). Templeton: 'this time it's different' is heard in every bubble, but '20% of the time things really are different.' Verdict: 'no one should go all-in without acknowledging that they face the risk of ruin if things go badly. But by the same token, no one should stay all-out ... A moderate position, applied with selectivity and prudence, seems like the best approach.' 'A Layman Thinks About AI' (11 Nov 2026): an AI investor must be right about technology, compute demand, competitive structure, beneficiaries, financing and timing - compounding probabilities (a 60% chance on each of four variables gives ~13%). Different claims need different correctness: a frontier-lab equity investor needs many things right; a data-centre lender under a long contract needs fewer (tenant credit, terms, power, residual value). 'intelligent investing is largely about price'; 'Two kinds of investors lose a lot of money: those who know nothing and those who know everything.' Quotes Buffett: 'you pay a very high price in the stock market for a cheery consensus. Uncertainty actually is the friend of the buyer of long-term values.' Actionable: for Indian AI/data-centre/power themes, size moderately and prefer positions whose thesis needs fewer things to go right.

Sources:

- https://www.oaktreecapital.com/insights/memo/a-layman-thinks-about-ai

VMM is covered by about 20 brokers, so the public P&L has no edge. Possible edges sit only in:
1. **Cost-line micro-drivers the sell side models as "% of sales"**, such as state minimum wages, outsourced security, and related-party logistics. These move with notifications and contracts, not with sales (see §2.3 and §2.4).
2. **Ground truth on store productivity in new geographies.** South/West stores and small-format stores are where the next 1,000 stores must work, and quarterly disclosures blur them.
3. **Supply overhang mechanics.** The PE sponsor still holds about 40%. Who absorbs the supply, and at what discount?

The rest of this file is the scaffolding needed to ask those three questions well.
